reason: The sources provide rich, verified details across multiple sites detailing the Apollo 11 quarantine protocols, facilities, and timeline.
story: When Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin, and Michael Collins splashed down in the Pacific Ocean in July 1969, their mission was not over. Fearing the crew might bring back deadly extraterrestrial microorganisms, NASA enforced an intensive 21-day quarantine. Right after recovery, the trio donned biological isolation suits and were sealed inside a converted Airstream trailer aboard the USS Hornet, where President Richard Nixon greeted them through a window. The trailer was flown to Houston, where the astronauts, their spacecraft, and 49 pounds of lunar samples were transferred into the airtight Lunar Receiving Laboratory. There, under the care of flight surgeons, the crew underwent daily medical checks, gave debriefings from behind glass, and even celebrated Armstrong's 39th birthday. As Michael Collins later joked, opening the capsule hatch at sea had already exposed the air anyway. On August 10, cleared of all space plagues, the heroes were finally released.
angle: To prevent an alien plague, Apollo 11 astronauts spent three weeks locked in a converted Airstream trailer and airtight bunker—even though opening the capsule hatch in the Pacific Ocean had already vented their air to Earth.

claims.claim: NASA placed Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin, and Michael Collins in a 21-day quarantine over concerns about potential lunar pathogens.
The initial Mobile Quarantine Facility was a converted Airstream trailer.
NASA contracted Melpar, Inc. to manufacture four Mobile Quarantine Facilities.
The Mobile Quarantine Facility was deployed aboard the prime recovery aircraft carrier USS Hornet.
President Richard Nixon greeted the Apollo 11 crew aboard the USS Hornet while they were sealed inside the Mobile Quarantine Facility.
The returning astronauts wore biological isolation garments before entering the mobile quarantine trailer.
The Mobile Quarantine Facility containing the astronauts was transported by air to Houston.
In Houston, the crew spent the remainder of their quarantine in the Lunar Receiving Laboratory at the Manned Spacecraft Center.
The Apollo 11 Command Module and lunar samples were kept in quarantine alongside the astronauts.
The Apollo 11 crew returned 49 pounds of lunar samples to Earth.
Neil Armstrong celebrated his 39th birthday while isolated in the quarantine facility.
Flight surgeon Dr. William Carpentier monitored the health status of the astronauts daily during quarantine.
Dr. Charles A. Berry opened the doors to release the astronauts from the Lunar Receiving Laboratory on the evening of August 10, 1969.
NASA lifted the lunar quarantine requirements after Apollo 14 once the Moon was confirmed to be sterile.
Michael Collins pointed out that opening the spacecraft hatch in the Pacific Ocean undermined the containment protocol by venting capsule air directly into the atmosphere.

disputed: Quarantine start time: Sources S2 and S3 state the 21-day quarantine began when the astronauts first contacted lunar material and sealed the lunar module hatch, while S5 and S6 describe the quarantine beginning at splashdown in the Pacific Ocean. A script should explain that the 21-day timeline was calculated from lunar surface operations, but physical isolation from Earth began at splashdown.

Support staff quarantine counts: S1 notes a doctor and engineer lived in the trailer, S3 mentions about 20 companions joined them in the LRL, S5 mentions over a dozen support staff, and S7 reports 24 NASA personnel were quarantined. A script should state generally that around two dozen support staff joined the crew in isolation.

Containment breach mechanics at sea: S3 and S6 cite Collins and Berry stating that opening the hatch released air into the atmosphere, while S7 claims the door was jettisoned and rushing air killed germs. A script should attribute Collins's observation directly to him as a notable flaw in the protocol.
